params._note: Every value carries its source. 'derived' = unit conversion or arithmetic on the cited values. 'assumption' = modelling choice, shown as such in the app.

plant_sizes_t_dry.source: design choice: small distributed units (5, 10 kt dry/y) versus larger central plants (25, 50, 100 kt dry/y), tested as scenarios

min_load_fraction.source: assumption: a plant is placed only if it can be filled to 80% of capacity

wheat_grain_yield_t_ha.source: FAO via Our World in Data, Saudi wheat yield 2015-2024 (low 2019, central 2024, high 2022) https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/wheat-yields?country=~SAU

straw_t_dry_per_ha.source: derived. Low/central: effective baled straw-to-grain ratio 0.4/0.5 (Drever 2021, in Lefebvre et al. 2023, Biochar 5:65, p.14) x grain yield low/central. High: IPCC 2006 Vol.4 Ch.11 Table 11.2 above-ground residue 1.51 x grain DM (0.89) + 0.52 t/ha at 6.80 t/ha, x 0.70 sustainable removal (Lefebvre 2023 s2.2.1)

collectable_fraction.source: 1.0 because straw_t_dry_per_ha is already the collectable amount (baled ratio or IPCC x 0.70 removal)

straw_dry_matter.source: Haulage only (straw supply is already a dry mass). Low: 15% small-grain moisture (Lefebvre et al. 2023, Biochar 5:65, p.14); high: Sedmihradska 2020 Table 3 (8.4% water); central 0.88 assumed between them

alfalfa_collectable_residue_t_ha.source: IPCC 2006 Table 11.2 footnote k: alfalfa residue is harvest losses and litter only (0.29 x yield), left in field; treated as not collectable

irrigation_mm_winter_only.source: Lopez Valencia et al. 2020, HESS 24:5251, p.5266: seasonal fields Q1/mean/Q3, water reaching the ground (Al Jawf 2015, satellite-model fusion)

irrigation_mm_year_round.source: Lopez Valencia et al. 2020, HESS 24:5251, p.5266: perennial (alfalfa/grass) fields Q1/mean/Q3

irrigation_mm_summer_crop.source: derived: half the perennial depth (irrigation_mm_year_round), the share this model already gives June-September for year-round fields. A June-October crop grows at peak evaporative demand, so the winter (seasonal-field) depth would understate it

pivot_application_efficiency.source: Multsch et al. 2013, GMD 6:1043 p.1049 (sprinkler 70%); Lopez Valencia et al. 2020 p.5256 (losses 12-20%, study adopts 20%)

pumping_lift_m.source: Al-Salamah & Nassar 2009, J. Appl. Sci. 9(19):3555: depth to water in Saq aquifer at Buraydah 90-138 m (2006). Central = midpoint (derived). Lower bound today: excludes later drawdown, pivot pressure and friction

pump_wire_to_water_eff.source: UGA Extension C965 Table 1: Nebraska performance standard 0.885 whp-h/kWh = 0.66 (derived). A well-run plant, so energy is a lower bound

grid_kgco2e_per_kwh.source: Ember via Our World in Data, Saudi Arabia carbon intensity of electricity, 2024 (691.95 g) and 2018 (702.88 g)

diesel_water_kwh_per_litre.source: UGA Extension C965 Table 1: Nebraska standard 12.5 whp-h/gal = 2.46 kWh of water work per litre (derived)

diesel_kgco2e_per_litre.source: DESNZ 2026 GHG conversion factors: diesel 2.66155 kg CO2e/L + well-to-tank 0.62409 (derived sum)

road_circuity.source: assumption: straight-line distance (lower bound); 1.4 is an unsourced sensitivity, flagged in the app

truck_kgco2e_per_tkm.source: DESNZ 2026 GHG conversion factors, freighting goods: articulated HGV >33 t 100% laden / average laden / all HGVs average laden

char_yield_dry.source: Sedmihradska et al. 2020, RAE 66(1), Tables 3-4: wheat and barley straw chars at 500-600 C, as received / feed dry matter: barley 600 C 28.2%, mean of four 30.7%, wheat 500 C 32.6% (derived)

char_c_org.source: Derived from Sedmihradska et al. 2020 Table 7 char carbon of four wheat/barley straw chars (64.7-67.2%; mean 66.1%) divided by an assumed total-to-organic carbon factor of 1.007 (lignocellulosic class, Enders et al. 2012 analogues): 0.643 / 0.656 / 0.667

cement_retention.source: Reported, not credited: in-service retention of char carbon in cementitious products, envelope 0.85-1.00 on 60-80 year horizons (Bartoli et al. 2020; Zou et al. 2025; Schmidt & Hagemann 2026, C-Sink Standard v3.3 s12.3). Credited removal uses the soil persistence model for cement too (Puro.earth 2025 v2 rule 6.2.4)

palms_per_ha.source: Low: Saudi 8-site average 100 trees/ha (AL-Omran & Eid 2019, Appl Water Sci, doi:10.1007/s13201-019-0936-6). Central: modern 9x9 m spacing 121/ha (FAO 2002, Date palm cultivation, Ch.VI). High: traditional ~6 m spacing 270/ha (FAO 2002 Table 40)

palm_residue_kg_dry_per_palm.source: Low: 15 kg/palm/yr (Al Yahya et al. 2021, Energies 14:6048, p.1; moisture basis not stated). Central: ~20 kg dry fronds/palm/yr (Chehma & Longo 2001, cited in Burezq & Davidson 2023, p.9). High: 28.3 kg oven-dry fronds/palm, derived from Nasser et al. 2016 (Energies 9:374) Table 1

palm_char_yield_dry.source: Usman et al. 2015 (J Anal Appl Pyrolysis, doi:10.1016/j.jaap.2015.08.016) Table 1: Saudi date palm waste biochar yield 32.4% at 500 C, 30.9% at 600 C

palm_char_c_org.source: Usman et al. 2015, JAAP, Table 1: Saudi date palm chars, organic carbon basis (total C 72.3-72.9% less inorganic C; Puro 2025 v2 rule 6.1.6), central 70.8%

layer_manure_kg_dry_per_hen.source: Layer manure, total solids per hen on hand per year: low USDA NRCS AWMFH (2008) Table 4-16(a) as transferred (4.37); central IPCC 2019 Table 10.13A Middle East high-productivity hens 5.21 kg VS / ASABE D384.2 VS:TS 0.735 = 7.09; high ASABE D384.2 as excreted (AWMFH Table 4-11(a)) 8.11

cattle_manure_kg_dry_per_head.source: Total solids per head per year: IPCC 2019 Table 10.13A Middle East dairy VS (low-productivity 1,163; mean 1,363 kg) / VS:TS 0.85 (USDA NRCS AWMFH Table 4-5 note 3); high: ASABE D384.2 total solids by animal class applied to the GASTAT 2024 herd (232,950 milking cows, dry cows, heifers, calves, bulls and 41,913 traditional cattle) = 2,135 (derived)

small_ruminant_manure_kg_dry_per_head.source: Total solids per head per year: IPCC 2019 Table 10.13A/10A.5 VS (sheep 93.9, goats 91.1 kg) / VS:TS (sheep 0.83, AWMFH Table 4-13; goats 0.822, Zhang et al. 2013 PLoS ONE 8:e66845); high uses VS 72% of TS (Hayat, Odeh & Elshurafa 2025, KAPSARC DP KS-2025-DP28, Table A6)

collectable_share_cattle.source: IPCC 2019 Tables 10A.6/10A.8 Middle East: 46% (dairy) / 42% (other cattle) deposited on pasture; collectable = 1 - pasture share (derived)

collectable_share_small_ruminants.source: IPCC 2019 Table 10A.9 Middle East sheep/goats: 50% pasture, 50% drylot; collectable = drylot share (derived)

collectable_share_poultry.source: IPCC 2019 Table 10A.9: broilers 100% 'poultry manure with litter', layers 0% pasture

litter_char_yield_dry.source: Bedded broiler litter: the 600 C measurements are 37% (Tsai & Chang 2021 s2.1) and 45.7% of dry feed (Song & Guo 2012, JAAP 94:138, Table 2); central 42.6% is Das et al. 2008 at 500 C, quoted in Song & Guo 2012 p.141

litter_char_c_org.source: Organic carbon of broiler-litter chars: low Song & Guo 2012 Table 2 TOC at 600 C (32.5%); central 39.6% and high 47% are assumed class values for carbonate-corrected litter chars (not measurements)

manure_char_yield_dry.source: Low: Cantrell et al. 2012, Bioresour. Technol., Table 2, dairy manure char at 700 C (35.0%); high: dairy interpolated to 500 C (46.4%); central 42.2% is an assumed class value at 600 C (Cantrell dairy and feedlot interpolated to 600 C give 40.7% and 37.6%)

manure_char_c_org.source: Woolf et al. 2021, Environ. Sci. Technol., Table 2: manure char carbon fraction 0.39 in all temperature classes; bounds 0.33-0.45 from in-window analogues

gastat_2024_totals.source: GASTAT Livestock Statistics 2024: sheep 22,055,779; goats 7,339,749; cattle 516 thousand; broiler barn capacity 274,069,031; layer capacity 55,101,080. Agricultural Statistics 2024: date palms 37,565,146. Livestock Statistics 2024 (Excel, published 20 Nov 2025) Tables 1-4, 2-1, 2-2, 3-1 to 3-3, 4-1: broilers produced 1,316,175,048 (2023: 1,165,355,341); broiler capacity 274,069,031 places is the most birds held on one day; eggs 8.42 bn table + 1.89 bn hatching; milking cows 232,950; camels 2,235,296

soil_temp_c.source: Annual mean soil temperature of the region of first use (Puro.earth 2025 v2 rule 6.2.4, also for char in cement): 30 C central, 25-33 C spanning Saudi regions (Lembrechts et al. 2022 soil bioclimatic dataset). Low estimate = hottest soil (least persistent)

puro_pf_table.source: Puro.earth Biochar Methodology 2025 v2, Table 6.1 p.101: persistence PF (%) = M - a x H/C_org over 200 years, M and a by soil temperature; a stream with H/C_org >= 0.70 is ineligible (rule 3.5.1)

h_c_org_straw.source: Derived: molar H/C_org = (H/1.008)/(C/12.011) from the C and H contents of four wheat/barley straw chars at 500-600 C in Sedmihradska et al. 2020 Table 7 (mean 0.391; bounds 0.322-0.528); persistence 0.697 / 0.708 / 0.730 at 33 / 30 / 25 C

h_c_org_fronds.source: Derived from Usman et al. 2015 Table 1 (Saudi date palm chars): H 2.11% at 500 C (1.74% at 600 C) over an assumed organic carbon of 70.8% gives H/C_org 0.358 (0.295); persistence 0.712 / 0.722 / 0.743

h_c_org_litter.source: Tsai & Chang 2021, Agronomy 11:1692, Table 1: bedded broiler litter char at 600 C, H/C 0.69 on TOTAL carbon (no inorganic-carbon correction). On the organic-carbon basis Puro requires it is about 0.70-0.73, at or above the 0.70 gate, so litter's eligibility is uncertain; credited here as eligible. Persistence 0.563 / 0.579 / 0.611

h_c_org_manure.source: Assumption: a class value for cattle-manure chars at 600 C (not a measurement). Measured manure chars in the Woolf et al. 2021 dataset span about 0.55-1.09 at 400-550 C (cow manure 0.72 at 550 C), so manure's eligibility is uncertain; credited here as eligible. Persistence 0.621 / 0.635 / 0.662

palm_frond_dry_matter.source: Haulage only: Usman et al. 2015 Table 1, date palm feedstock moisture 7.6%

litter_dry_matter.source: Haulage only: USDA NRCS AWMFH (2008) Table 4-16(a), broiler litter as removed, 31% moisture / 70% solids; applied to the whole poultry stream, although layer manure (about a third of it) is wetter

manure_dry_matter.source: Haulage only: USDA NRCS AWMFH (2008) Table 4-16(a), dairy manure scraped from earthen lots, 54% moisture / 46% solids

broiler_litter_kg_dry_per_bird.source: Bedded broiler litter per bird produced (applied to GASTAT 2024 birds produced, 1,316,175,048): low Coufal et al. 2006, Poultry Sci. 85:398 (228 g dry litter per kg live weight per flock x 1.40 kg); central Berry 1997 via MSU Ext. P3601 Table 2 (0.311 kg DM per kg live weight x 1.40 kg); high all excreted solids, IPCC 2019 Table 10.13A Middle East broilers (0.52 kg VS over 42 d) / ASABE D384.2 VS:TS 0.75 + GASTAT 2023 wood shavings 0.05 kg. Market live weight 1.40 kg (USDA FAS GAIN 2006)

layers_on_hand.source: Laying hens: GASTAT 2024 eggs (8,420,841,886 table + 1,890,623,330 hatching) / 286 eggs per layer on hand (USDA NASS Chickens and Eggs 2023, transferred) = 36.05 M; high = GASTAT layer capacity 55.10 M (includes parent and grandparent flocks)

official_sources.G24: GASTAT Agricultural Statistics 2024 (published 30 Nov 2025), https://www.stats.gov.sa/en/statistics-tabs?tab=436312&category=124583 ; tables 1-3 (wheat), 1-4 (fodder), 5-1 (date palms)
official_sources.M24: MEWA Statistical Book 2024 (Arabic, Dec 2025), https://www.mewa.gov.sa/ar/InformationCenter/Researchs/Reports/GeneralReports/TheStatisticalBook.pdf ; pp.62-63 agricultural groundwater use by region
official_sources.lift: Static depth to groundwater (no pumping levels published); see lift_m sources per region

Al-Jouf.source: Saq 65-297 m (Ahmed et al. 2015, Environ Earth Sci 74:1303, Table 1); Sakaka static 200 m (1979) and Tawil max 250 m bgl (ESCWA-BGR 2013 Ch.13 p.360, Ch.17 p.429)

Tabuk.source: ESCWA-BGR 2013 Ch.10 pp.307-310: most levels 50-150 m bgl, around 200 m bgl

Hail.source: Kahal 2024, JKSUS doi:10.1016/j.jksus.2024.103384 s2.1: ~220 m around Hail city, 54 m toward the centre; central = midpoint (derived)

Qassim.source: Al-Salamah & Nassar 2009, J Appl Sci 9(19):3555: Saq at Buraydah 90-138 m (2006)

Riyadh.source: Alharbi 2023, JKSUS doi:10.1016/j.jksus.2023.102847: Biyadh 92-130 m (Wadi Sahba/Al-Kharj); 91-111 m (preprint)

WadiDawasir.source: ESCWA-BGR 2013 Ch.11 pp.326-327: Wajid ~150 m bgl, 90-100 m west of Wadi ad-Dawasir; central = midpoint (derived)

_fallback.source: No regional depth found (Eastern, Northern Borders); Qassim range used and flagged

lift._shield: Arabian Shield regions (Makkah, Madinah, Asir, Jazan, Najran, Al-Baha): shallow alluvial or rainfed/spate systems; pumping energy not estimated

mwan.confidence_legend: estimation based on assumptions from international benchmarks
mwan.streams_basis: MWAN-based estimates for 2030 back-cast to 2024 at 1.44%/yr; wet or dry not stated
mwan.source: MWAN (National Center for Waste Management), national waste inventory, National Waste Management Strategy (2023)

fodder_halt.source: MEWA news release, 7 Jumada I 1448 AH: halt of perennial fodder cultivation in the sedimentary-shelf regions from 16 November 2026; seasonal fodder allowed under licence (Council of Ministers Resolution No. 66, per Argaam, 26 Jan 2026)
